annotations.title: Great shal be the glorie.
annotations.text: [1] VVhen according to the prophets exhortation the temple vvas built againe, Eſdras ch. 3. v 12. writeth, that ſuch ancient men as had ſene the former, lamented, becauſe this nevv one vvas not ſo excellent as the former had bene, which is alſo clere by other places of holie ſcripture. For amongſt other differences, Salomons temple had in height, and in breadth, an hundred and twentie cubites 2 Paral. 3. v. 4. this nevv temple had but ſixtie cubites. 1 Eſd. 6. v 3. Likevviſe Salomons temple vvas built of ſtones hevved and perfectly polished, 3. Reg 6. v. 7. vvhich vvere alſo couered on the innerſide vvith ſeeling vvorke of ceder vvood. v 18. This nevv temple vvas built of rugh and vnpolished ſtones. 1. Eſd. 5. v. 8 As for the ſame temple long after enlarged and adorned by Herod, it continued not long in that ſtate, [2] & the chiefeſt glorie therof vvas by our Sauiours preſence therin, when he was preſented by his mother, and ioyfully receiued into the armes of Simeon, and often preached there. And therfore S. Auguſtin proueth li. 18. c. 45 ciuit. that the prophet here foresheweth the glorie of Chriſts myſtical temple, faithful Chriſtian ſoules of al nations, in whom God dwelleth by grace of the new Teſtament, farre more glorious in liuing ſtones, then that temple which king Salomon built, or that which was reſtored after the captiuitie.

notes.text: The temple restored after the captiuitie was not so glorious as that which Salomon built.
But Christs Church of the new Testament in which he dwelleth spiritually farre excelleth the material temple.
